_comment: Human adjudication of the benign-slice HIGH/CRITICAL findings. run.py deliberately does NOT write this: the false-positive rate is a human judgement, and a harness that labelled its own findings would be measuring nothing. Verdict rule (see triage.md): rate = false_positive / adjudicated; ambiguous counts in the denominator only.
tuned_note: Corpus-side fix, no rule change. The 2026-08-24 run left two false positives and one ambiguous verdict, all three attributable to the corpus builder rather than to any rule: fetch_registry._to_config() converted remotes[0] only, so a server publishing an anonymous or login entry point first lost its declared auth in conversion and was handed to the scanner as a credential-less config. _to_config() was fixed at the time, but the committed manifest predated the fix and RESULTS.md deliberately did not bundle the regeneration into a precision fix. This run regenerates the manifest from the same cached 2026-07-26 registry snapshot, so the slice size (536) and the fetch date are unchanged and the two runs are directly comparable. Exactly 3 of 1,641 configs change and 0 auth_modes change; the patched manifest was asserted equal to a full re-derivation. AAK-MCP-001 is unmodified - it was correct about every config it was handed. The single remaining HIGH/CRITICAL finding is the true positive that has been stable across every run since 2026-07-20.
